headline_findings: Resolve-then-Range-GET with ETag pinning is the stable plain-HTTP path; HEAD gives LFS-sha256 etag, size and commit hash.
Multi-GB weights now live on the Xet CAS backend: plain resolve-URL follows can stall at 0 bytes; real Xet needs reconstruction-API + signed xorb fetches.
hf-hub Rust crate 1.0.0 (Jul 2026) gives Cerebro async/blocking search, listing, resume and Xet transfers with a Python-compatible cache.
Gated repos need user token + browser Agree flow; app must show licence/gated state before download and store tokens in OS keychain.
Rate limits are per-bucket over 5-min windows with 429 + RateLimit headers; always send HF_TOKEN and back off; hf cache verify fills the no-on-download-hash gap.

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent: single-stream Range resume suits laptop links; generous timeouts beat default 10s on slow Wi-Fi.
items.harness_integration: HEAD resolve URL for etag/size/commit; GET with Range to .part file; atomic rename; file lock; truncate+restart if server ignores Range (200 without Content-Range).
items.name: Resolve-URL + ETag + Range resume
items.quality_cost: None with correct Range handling; naive resume against gzip/CDN responses corrupts progress accounting (fixed PR #4209).
items.reported_gain: Resume avoids full multi-GB restart after interrupt; correctness not throughput. HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT default 10s, raise on slow links.
items.what: HEAD /{ns}/{repo}/resolve/{rev}/{path} for ETag/size/commit, then resumable Range GET to .incomplete + rename.

items.fit_reference_machine: Mixed: best speed on good links via adaptive concurrency; HP mode needs 64GB RAM so keep defaults on 32GB laptop.
items.harness_integration: Prefer Xet-capable dependency (hf-hub 1.x/xet-core) or shell hf download; support HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 fallback with stall warning.
items.name: hf_xet Xet CAS download path
items.quality_cost: Same bytes out; dedup can share chunks across related files. Interrupts may restart from 0 unlike LFS resume.
items.reported_gain: Chunk-level dedup + adaptive concurrency saturate fast links; no published batch-1 laptop tok/s style figure, treat as transfer-time win only.
items.what: Default since huggingface_hub 0.32.0: CAS reconstruction query + signed multi-range xorb fetch + chunk reassembly.
items.where_implemented: hf-xet package bundled with huggingface_hub>=0.32.0; xet-core Rust crates; HF_XET_* env vars

items.fit_reference_machine: Directly explains the observed 0-byte stall on this laptop: bridge fallback hangs where CAS path proceeds.
items.harness_integration: Read X-Xet-Hash on resolve HEAD; if Xet-backed and no Xet client, warn user and offer hf download/hfrs instead of hanging.
items.name: Xet resolve-redirect vs CAS trap
items.quality_cost: Bridge bytes are identical when it works; failure mode is a hang, not wrong bytes.
items.reported_gain: No gain; diagnostic rule. MUST NOT follow 302 for Xet protocol use; signed xorb URLs are short-lived, never cache them.
items.what: Following a resolve-URL 302 uses the legacy LFS-compat bridge (can stall at 0B); Xet protocol needs the reconstruction API.
items.where_implemented: Xet spec docs/xet/file-id.md; CAS discovery via /xet-read-token (cas-server.xethub.hf.co)

items.harness_integration: Do not implement; if encountered in old docs, map to hf_xet defaults or plain Range resume.

items.quality_cost: No resume, no proxies, weaker error handling by design.
items.reported_gain: Up to ~1GB/s claimed on high-bandwidth machines (unverified, datacenter-class); deprecated, throughput not transferable to laptop.
items.what: Deprecated Rust parallel-range downloader (HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER); replaced by hf_xet on the Xet backend.
items.where_implemented: hf_transfer crate; deprecated env var HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER in huggingface_hub

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: post-download sha256 of a 20-40GB GGUF takes minutes on NVMe; run as opt-in gate, not default.
items.harness_integration: Always size-check; offer verify toggle comparing sha256 vs LFS etag (quality gate); never load unverified weights silently.
items.name: LFS-sha256 checksums + hf cache verify
items.quality_cost: Verification is pure win for integrity; costs a full re-read. No on-download hash by design (Dec 2025 decision).
items.reported_gain: No speed gain; integrity gain. blobs/<etag> identity means corrupt files detectable; hf cache verify added Oct 2025 (PR #3461).
items.what: Blob filename IS the sha256 (LFS) or git-sha1; hf cache verify recomputes and reports mismatches.
items.where_implemented: huggingface_hub cache layout; hf cache verify CLI; verify_repo_checksums API
